item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption surveyed community views about corruption, its work and willingness to report wrongdoing.
item.support: The CAS is used to gauge the public’s perception of corruption and of the ICAC

item.text: The 2015 telephone survey included 501 NSW adults, with quotas for age, gender and location.
item.support: A total of 501 eligible people agreed to participate.

item.text: The Commission found that most respondents regarded public sector corruption as a community problem and half believed it affected them or their families.
item.support: Most respondents reported that corruption in the NSW public sector is a problem for the community.

item.text: The Commission found that most respondents were willing to report serious corruption, with overall willingness broadly stable since the previous survey.
item.support: Most respondents indicated that they were willing to report serious public sector corruption to the ICAC

item.text: The Commission suggests further education for public employees and forums for suppliers about corruption and reporting.
item.support: These findings suggest that public sector employees may benefit from further training and education

item.quote: Most respondents reported that corruption in the NSW public sector is a problem for the community.
Half of the survey respondents indicated that corruption affects them or their families.
